outline.chapter_title: Introduction to DeepSeekMath and Mathematical Reasoning
outline.description: Introduces the challenges of mathematical reasoning for language models, the motivation behind DeepSeekMath, and a high-level overview of its architecture, contributions, and evaluation metrics.
subtopics: The Challenge of Mathematical Reasoning in AI
The Gap Between Open-Source and Closed-Source LLMs
Overview of DeepSeekMath: Base, Instruct, and RL Models
Key Contributions: Data Pipeline and GRPO
Summary of Evaluation Benchmarks (English, Chinese, Formal Math, and General Reasoning)

outline.chapter_title: Data Collection and the DeepSeekMath Corpus
outline.description: Details the methodology for creating a large-scale, high-quality mathematical pre-training corpus from Common Crawl, including the iterative fastText classification pipeline and decontamination procedures.
subtopics: The Need for High-Quality Math Web Data
Initial Seed Corpus and fastText Classifier Training
The Iterative Data Collection Pipeline
Domain-Based Expansion and Human Annotation
Data Decontamination Techniques
Validating Corpus Quality Against Existing Datasets

outline.description: Explains the pre-training process of the DeepSeekMath-Base 7B model, starting from a code-trained model, and evaluates its performance across mathematical, formal, and general reasoning tasks.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
Data Distribution and Training Configuration
Performance on Step-by-Step Mathematical Reasoning
Tool-Integrated Mathematical Problem Solving
Formal Mathematics and Theorem Proving
General Natural Language Understanding and Code Performance

outline.description: Covers the creation of the mathematical instruction-tuning dataset using various reasoning formats and the training and evaluation of the DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B model.
subtopics: SFT Data Curation: Chain-of-Thought (CoT), Program-of-Thought (PoT), and Tool-Integrated Reasoning
English and Chinese Mathematical Datasets
Training Configuration for DeepSeekMath-Instruct
Evaluation Without Tool Use
Evaluation With Tool Integration
Benchmarking Against Open-Source and Proprietary Models

outline.description: Introduces GRPO, a variant of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), detailing its mathematical formulation, memory efficiency advantages, and applications in outcome and process supervision.
subtopics: Limitations of PPO in LLM Reinforcement Learning
The GRPO Algorithm and Mathematical Formulation
Group Relative Advantage Estimation
Outcome Supervision RL with GRPO
Process Supervision RL with GRPO
Iterative RL with GRPO

outline.description: Details the application of GRPO to train DeepSeekMath-RL, the training setup, and the evaluation results demonstrating the effectiveness of RL on both in-domain and out-of-domain tasks.
subtopics: Training Setup for DeepSeekMath-RL
Reward Model Construction and Training
Performance on In-Domain Tasks (GSM8K and MATH)
Out-of-Domain Performance Enhancements
Comparative Analysis with SFT and Other Models

outline.description: Discusses key empirical findings from pre-training experiments, specifically the impact of code training on math reasoning and the surprising ineffectiveness of arXiv papers.
subtopics: The Hypothesis: Does Code Training Improve Reasoning?
Two-Stage vs. One-Stage Training Paradigms
Impact of Code Training on Tool-Use and Non-Tool-Use Math
Catastrophic Forgetting and Mitigation Strategies
Evaluating the Efficacy of ArXiv Papers for Math Pre-Training

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm for Reinforcement Learning
outline.description: Provides a unified paradigm to understand various training methods (SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO), explains why RL improves performance, and outlines future directions for more effective RL.
subtopics: The Unified Paradigm: Data Source, Reward Function, and Algorithm
Analysis of Data Source: Online vs. Offline Sampling
Analysis of Gradient Coefficients: Rule vs. Model Rewards
Why RL Works: Pass@K vs. Maj@K Accuracy
Future Directions: Advanced Sampling, Robust Algorithms, and Reward Models

outline.description: Summarizes the achievements of DeepSeekMath, acknowledges its limitations in areas like geometry and few-shot learning, and discusses the broader implications of the research.
subtopics: Summary of DeepSeekMath's Achievements
Limitations in Geometry, Theorem Proving, and Few-Shot Learning
Data Selection Bias and Model Scale Constraints
Future Work in Data Engineering and RL Techniques
